purpose: Headless whole-file build of the genuine gameplay code and the genuine renderer, driven through the vanilla -playdemo path and R_RenderPlayerView after every dumped tic; run in CI on synthetic WADs with the synthetic graphics PWAD and locally on a real IWAD. Expected frames come from the genuine code, never from Rust output.

excluded.p_saveg_c: aborting stubs for its eight P_(Un)Archive* functions and save_p
excluded.r_main_extract: not used: r_main.c is compiled whole

variant_notes.address: run with ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 (leak detection disabled; not LeakSanitizer coverage); -fno-sanitize=alignment because z_zone.c rounds block sizes to 4 (z_zone.c:195) while the LP64 memblock_t needs 8-byte alignment

abi_adapters.reason: P_GroupLines: linebuffer holds total line_t pointers (8 bytes each on LP64); total*4 overruns the zone block and Z_CheckHeap (g_game.c:488) calls I_Error.
On-disk maptexture_t: a 4-byte field as on the 32-bit original, so patchcount is at byte 20 and patches at 22 (the driver checks the generated layout probe before running).
R_InitTextures: textures is a pointer array (texture_t**).
R_InitColormaps truncates a pointer to int; the runner does not call it, the file is adapted so it compiles LP64-clean (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line).

Z_ChangeTag: the owner test truncates the 64-bit user pointer to 32 bits, so a valid owner whose address has small low 32 bits (observed under ASan on the CI runner: W_CacheLumpNum re-caching the one patch lump) raises "an owner is required for purgable blocks"; the 32-bit original compares the whole pointer, which uintptr_t does on LP64 (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line).

sanitizer_adapters.reason: P_SpawnPlayer: ANG45 * q overflows int for quotients outside -4..3; the original targets wrap it modulo 2^32, which the unsigned product computes (same statement form as p_mobj.c:794).
P_SpawnMapThing: the declared M3h9b adapter (tools/reference/m3h9b_reference.py SANITIZER_ADAPTERS[0]).
P_RadiusAttack: the declared M3h9b adapter (tools/reference/m3h9b_reference.py SANITIZER_ADAPTERS[1]).

A_PosAttack: `int angle` holds the actor angle (angle_t converted to int) and the spread is added in int, which overflows for angles near the int limits; the original targets wrap it modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does (the P_Random subexpression is unchanged). Needed: the overflow build reports this statement on the synthetic chaos script.
A_SPosAttack: the same int sum as p_enemy.c:816; declared for robustness.
A_CPosAttack: the same int sum as p_enemy.c:816; declared for robustness.

P_DamageMobj: a telefrag (PIT_StompThing, p_map.c:105) passes damage 10000, so the int product damage*(FRACUNIT>>3)*100 overflows (it does for any damage >= 2622). The genuine strict (-fwrapv) and strict32 builds wrap it modulo 2^32 to -397,934,592 before the signed division; the unsigned product computes the same wrapped value without undefined behaviour and the (int) conversion is modulo on GCC; the division stays signed (decision I3, docs/M4B_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md section 2 T8.10).

render_abi_adapters.reason: R_InitTranslationTables truncates a pointer to int before aligning it to 256 (as r_data.c:642 does for colormaps); on LP64 the truncated pointer is invalid. intptr_t keeps the whole pointer (stdint.h comes from -include on the command line); strict32 compiles the genuine text, where int and pointers have the same width.

render_sanitizer_adapters.reason: R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle: finesine has 10240 entries (tables.c:584) and finetangent, 4096, immediately precedes it (tables.c:67; the driver checks this layout in strict and strict32), so the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finetangent[4096 + i] for a negative index i (from -4096 to -1: `int angleb>>ANGLETOFINESHIFT` of an angle sum whose top bit is set); the address build puts a redzone between the arrays and -fsanitize=bounds reports the index, so the adapter reads that element explicitly (finetangent[FINEANGLES/2 + i]). The three-variant frame identity shows it is the same value. Same form as r_main.c:485; declared for robustness.

R_ScaleFromGlobalAngle: finesine has 10240 entries (tables.c:584) and finetangent, 4096, immediately precedes it (tables.c:67; the driver checks this layout in strict and strict32), so the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finetangent[4096 + i] for a negative index i (from -4096 to -1: `int angleb>>ANGLETOFINESHIFT` of an angle sum whose top bit is set); the address build puts a redzone between the arrays and -fsanitize=bounds reports the index, so the adapter reads that element explicitly (finetangent[FINEANGLES/2 + i]). The three-variant frame identity shows it is the same value. Observed: index -218 on the BINF1 synthetic script in the Phase 1 prototype.

R_RenderSegLoop: angle is 0..8191 (an angle_t shifted right by ANGLETOFINESHIFT) while finetangent has 4096 entries; the genuine strict and strict32 builds read finesine[angle - 4096] for angle >= 4096 (finesine follows finetangent, tables.c:67, 584; checked by the driver), and the difference rw_offset - FixedMul(...) wraps modulo 2^32 under -fwrapv (observed overflow -70518787 - 2082184609 on TSPLIT, BVB1 and BARON1 in the prototype). The adapter reads the element explicitly and subtracts in unsigned arithmetic, converted back to fixed_t (modulo on GCC).

R_StoreWallRange: abs of an int difference that can be INT_MIN (observed on BTUNNEL in the prototype); the genuine strict and strict32 abs returns INT_MIN, which converts to 0x80000000 in the angle_t offsetangle; the adapter computes that value as an unsigned negation without the signed overflow.

R_StoreWallRange: the texture-mid sum overflows 32 bits on a high wall with a large row offset (observed in the address build on the real-map scripts M8IDLE and M8IDLE3 in the prototype, owner ruling on R12); the genuine strict and strict32 builds wrap it modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does.
R_StoreWallRange: as r_segs.c:603 for the lower texture (observed in the address build on the real-map script M9WALK in the prototype); the genuine builds wrap modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does.

R_DrawPlanes: index SCREENWIDTH of byte top[SCREENWIDTH]; visplane_t puts pad2 right after top (r_defs.h), which absorbs the write in every build. -fsanitize=bounds reports the array index; the subscript through a byte pointer is the same store.
R_DrawPlanes: index -1 of top[] lands in pad1 (r_defs.h); the same store through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads top[minx-1] (pad1, 0xff); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads bottom[minx-1] (pad3, 0 from static storage); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads top[maxx+1] (pad2, 0xff); the same load through a byte pointer.
R_DrawPlanes: reads bottom[maxx+1] (pad4, 0); the same load through a byte pointer.

R_DrawSpan: the texture coordinate sum overflows (observed -2145453427 + -11386560 on TELE1, SAWBITE, TELEZ, BOSS2, BTUNNEL in the prototype); only its low bits index the flat (r_draw.c:548-557); the genuine strict and strict32 builds wrap modulo 2^32, as the unsigned sum does. Line-keyed: r_draw.c:682 has the same text.
R_DrawSpan: as r_draw.c:559 for the other coordinate; the genuine builds wrap modulo 2^32. Line-keyed: the text is also a prefix of r_draw.c:683 (which ends with a space).
R_DrawSpanLow: the same sum as r_draw.c:559 (declared for robustness; low detail is refused, decision R2). Line-keyed: r_draw.c:559 has the same text.
R_DrawSpanLow: as r_draw.c:560 (declared for robustness; low detail is refused).

1 as D_CheckNetGame sets it (d_net.c:567-592); divisor at g_game.c:656.

builds local ticcmds from events (none headless) and polls the network; called four times by R_RenderPlayerView (r_main.c:881-897); single-player demo playback overwrites the console player's ticcmd from the demo (g_game.c:664-667).
malloc and memset 0, as vanilla; V_Init allocates the four screens with it (v_video.c:489).
the view size R_Init passes to R_SetViewSize (r_main.c:783; default 9, m_misc.c:279); the driver sets it from --screenblocks.
the detail R_Init passes to R_SetViewSize (default 0, m_misc.c:280); the driver accepts 0 only (low detail is refused, decision R2).

driver_behaviour: The demo header selects skill, episode and map (g_game.c:1596-1598); the driver has no map argument.
I_Quit (vanilla exit(0), i_system.c:116-124) sets a flag and longjmps to the driver, so no statement after the call in G_CheckDemoStatus or G_Ticker runs, as with exit.

After each dumped tic the driver stops if gameaction is ga_completed, ga_victory or ga_worlddone (end=exit, set during P_Ticker by G_ExitLevel/G_SecretExitLevel, g_game.c:1002-1018): G_Ticker handles gameaction before reading the next ticcmd (g_game.c:617-652, 656-669), so the next call would run G_DoCompleted and enter the intermission (g_game.c:1133-1140), which the runner does not model; a demo that reaches its marker ends end=marker. WI_Start still aborts as a safety net.

After each dumped tic the driver also stops if a player in the game is PST_REBORN (end=reborn; P_DeathThink on BT_USE, p_user.c:227-228): the next G_Ticker would run its reborn loop (g_game.c:612-614), G_DoReborn would set ga_loadlevel (g_game.c:924-931) and the level would reload (g_game.c:621-623), outside the admitted domain (decision G11).
After every tic the driver calls the genuine Z_CheckHeap (z_zone.c:399-420), a read-only walk of the zone; vanilla calls it only in G_DoLoadLevel (g_game.c:488).

Linker-level observers (-Wl,--wrap): P_AddThinker gives each thinker a serial (T rows), P_SetThingPosition gives the thing a link serial (the global link order is the ascending current link serial), Z_Free of a known thinker records it as freed since the previous dump (K rows, in free order) and, for a removed mobj, a copy of the mobj taken before the genuine free (RM rows); P_InitThinkers (after Z_FreeTags at level setup) drops every entry (K rows with seq -1). K rows also carry adds, the P_AddThinker count at the free; a pending mobj (R row) is followed by an RR row with its M columns. Each of these wrappers only records and then calls the genuine function.

ZeroFill: the Z_Malloc wrapper zero-fills every block after the genuine allocation. Only values the original leaves undefined change: plat_t.count (EV_DoPlat, p_plats.c:173; read only in waiting after being set, p_plats.c:75, 84, 113, 120) and floormove_t.newspecial (EV_DoFloor, p_floor.c:282; set and read only for lowerAndChange and donutRaise, p_floor.c:231, 242, 422, 433, p_spec.c:1203) made the strict and address dumps differ. lowerAndChange without a neighbour at the destination height reads newspecial and texture uninitialised in vanilla (p_floor.c:242-243); the fill makes them 0 there.

HU_Ticker records players[consoleplayer].message for the dump and clears it as vanilla does with the default show_messages 1; P rows report it as 0 (NULL), the 1-based index of the d_englsh.h GOTARMOR..GOTSHOTGUN2 pickup string (1..37), 38..40 for the locked-door strings PD_BLUEK, PD_YELLOWK, PD_REDK (d_englsh.h:128-130, assigned at p_doors.c:378, 392, 405; added for M4a), 41 for G_Ticker's turbo message (sprintf ("%s is turbo!", player_names[0]) as g_game.c:675-678 builds it, assigned when forwardmove > TURBOTHRESHOLD on every 128th gametic; added for M4a step 8), or -1 (any other).
--selftest-extra-draw TIC calls the public P_Random () once before G_Ticker of tic TIC (test only).
The zone is 6 MiB (vanilla mb_used, i_system.c:51) unless --zone-mb is given.

H rows end with secretexit (added for M4a): g_game.c's boolean secretexit (g_game.c:999), set by G_SecretExitLevel (g_game.c:1009-1018) and cleared by G_ExitLevel (g_game.c:1002-1006). New columns are appended at the end of their rows so every earlier column keeps its position.

R rows carry fn and sector (added for M4a): a -Wl,--wrap=P_RemoveThinker observer records, before the genuine P_RemoveThinker (p_tick.c:80-84) overwrites the function pointer, the kind of a removed non-mobj thinker (1 T_VerticalDoor, 2 T_PlatRaise, 3 T_MoveFloor, 4 T_MoveCeiling, 0 other) and its sector index, so a mover created and removed within one tic keeps its sector for the encoder; -1 when unknown.

M4b runner (tools/reference/m4b_build.py): the M4a driver text unchanged (no new dump column); one more declared sanitizer adapter, p_inter.c:817 (the telefrag thrust product in unsigned arithmetic), applied to the overflow and address builds only; strict and strict32 compile the genuine text.

M5a runner (tools/reference/m5a_build.py; decisions R1-R16 of docs/M5A_REFERENCE_INVESTIGATION.md): the M4a driver text forked into tools/reference/m5a_driver.c; the 34 genuine files of the M4b runner with its ABI and sanitizer adapters, plus the genuine renderer whole (r_main.c r_bsp.c r_segs.c r_plane.c r_things.c r_draw.c v_video.c; the r_main.c extract is not used) and tools/reference/m5a_stubs.c.

Sequence (M5a): V_Init (d_main.c:1012); Z_Init; W_InitMultipleFiles over the --wad files (map WAD, tests/reference/m5a_gfx.wad, demo lump); gamemode = registered; R_Init (d_main.c:1095: R_InitData = textures, flats, sprite lumps, colormaps; R_SetViewSize (screenblocks, 0); R_InitPlanes; R_InitLightTables; R_InitSkyMap; R_InitTranslationTables); P_InitSwitchList; P_InitPicAnims; R_InitSprites on a NUMSPRITES+1 copy of sprnames with an explicit NULL terminator (info.c:40-55 has no terminator, R_InitSpriteDefs counts to NULL, r_things.c:191; equivalent to vanilla P_Init when the word after sprnames is NULL); D_CheckNetGame single-player values; singledemo; G_DeferedPlayDemo; G_DoPlayDemo; R_ExecuteSetViewSize (the first D_Display, d_main.c:215-217); dump "load"; then { G_Ticker; gametic++; Z_CheckHeap; dump; view record; render } per tic.

Rendering (decision R8): with --render every, R_RenderPlayerView (&players[displayplayer]) after the dump of every dumped tic and before the stop checks, as D_Display does once per tic with one tic per frame (d_main.c:267-268); the load (gametic 0) is never rendered, end=exit and end=reborn tics are, the end=marker tic has no frame. The frame is screens[0] right after R_RenderPlayerView: screens[0] starts zeroed (I_AllocLow), fuzzpos starts 0 in a fresh process and neither is ever reset; no status bar, HUD, border, menu or palette is drawn. --render none (the default) never renders.

L rows print line_t.flags with ML_MAPPED (256, doomdata.h:135) cleared (decision R5): R_StoreWallRange sets it on every wall it stores (r_segs.c:398) and only the automap (am_map.c:1128) and savegames (p_saveg.c:141) read it; the newly mapped lines of each frame travel in the frame stream (M rows). --no-mask-mapped (diagnostic) prints the genuine value.

Frame stream (--frames FILE, schema DOOM-M5A-FRAMES-v1, row kinds in frame_row_kinds): per frame the SHA-256 of the 64,000 bytes of screens[0] computed in the driver (FIPS 180-4, written for the driver), the SHA-256 with the tracker-flagged columns zeroed, fuzzpos, the mapped-line count, the counters lastvisplane-visplanes, ds_p-drawsegs, vissprite_p-vissprites, lastopening-openings, the solidsegs peak, the R_StoreWallRange calls dropped at MAXDRAWSEGS, whether R_NewVisSprite returned overflowsprite (a 0x5a sentinel in that write-only sink, r_things.c:326-331) and whether a column source was unidentified; M rows (newly mapped lines), U rows (tracker-flagged columns with their origins), N rows (origin names), O rows (limit witnesses), E rows (I_Error during a frame). --frames-raw DIR writes frame_NNNNN.raw per frame.

Read-provenance tracker (decision R4 and its owner ruling): -Wl,--wrap observers of R_DrawColumn, R_DrawFuzzColumn and R_DrawSpan recompute every source index the genuine loop reads (r_draw.c:132-146) and classify it against the source block (the last R_GetColumn composite, or the cache block of the last W_CacheLumpNum lump) and, for composites, a written-byte mask replicated from R_GenerateLookup and R_DrawColumnInCache (r_data.c:184-216, 351-372) using W_ReadLump (never the zone); a per-pixel taint follows the never-cleared screen (spans clear it, fuzz copies it from the pixel it reads). Columns holding a tainted pixel are the frame's non-comparable columns; an unidentified source makes the whole frame non-comparable. The wrappers read genuine state only and then call the genuine drawer.

View record (--view FILE, schema DOOM-M5A-VIEW-v1, decision R6): per dumped tic, after the dump, the player's mobj x, y and angle, viewz, viewheight, deltaviewheight, bob, onground (p_user.c:51), extralight, fixedcolormap, the invisibility power, both psprites (state, tics, sx, sy) and the player's sector and light level, and the non-identity flat and texture translations (A rows).

Limits (decision R3): MAXDRAWSEGS and MAXVISSPRITES drop silently in the genuine code (r_segs.c:386-387, r_things.c:330-331) and are counted in the frame stream; R_FindPlane calls I_Error past MAXVISPLANES (r_plane.c:245-246) and R_DrawPlanes past MAXVISPLANES or MAXOPENINGS (r_plane.c:380-386), which the stub reports in an E row before it aborts; a write past visplanes (R_CheckPlane, r_plane.c:313-317), openings (R_StoreWallRange) or solidsegs (R_ClipSolidWallSegment, r_bsp.c:122-133), detected by the R_CheckPlane and R_StoreWallRange observers, is reported in an O row with its witness name and ends the run after that frame with end=refused.

Configurations (decision R2): --screenblocks 3..11; --detail 1 is refused with status 8 before anything loads (low detail is a known limitation); R_DrawColumnLow, R_DrawSpanLow and R_DrawTranslatedColumn (player colour translation, refused by decision R1) abort if ever reached.
--selftest-pixel TIC X Y (test only) flips the low bit of one screens[0] pixel right after R_RenderPlayerView of tic TIC, before the frame is hashed; it never touches genuine code text.

Table layout (decision R12): in strict and strict32 (no table adapters) the driver refuses to run (status 9) unless finesine starts right after finetangent (tables.c:67, 584), the layout the genuine out-of-range reads of r_main.c:484-485 and r_segs.c:266 rely on.
